clue.text: Pledge offered by a company of funeral directors

definitions.meaning: a solemn binding promise
read literally, a business whose trade is burying the dead

explanation.definitionFit: A binding promise is a firm commitment, and a funeral parlour's business could punningly be called the same.

clue.text: Journeyman identified as one of the Reds under the bed

definitions.meaning: taken literally, a man who goes on a journey alongside another

definitions.text: one of the Reds under the bed
definitions.meaning: a Communist sympathiser, the hidden enemy of Cold War paranoia

explanation.definitionFit: A companion on a journey is a fellow voyager; the same phrase was used for a non-member sympathetic to Communism.

clue.text: Democrat initially put in racial reforms of a fundamental nature

indicators.note: put in tells us one piece is placed inside another
reforms says the letters of racial are reshaped into a new order
initially picks out just the opening letter of the word Democrat

explanation.surface: A Democrat politician begins sweeping changes to race policy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reforms' rearranges RACIAL to RAICAL; 'put in' places D (the first letter, from 'initially') inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Radical comes from the Latin for root, so a radical change goes to the basic nature of things.

clue.text: Not a new American edition

explanation.surface: A copy that is not the latest US printing of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Something second-hand, not fresh from the shop, has had an owner before.

clue.text: Ruin for a British ministry going to the city of Paris

indicators.note: going to places one piece directly before the other

parts.note: the DES was the Department of Education and Science, a former UK government department
Paris, prince of Troy in Greek legend, belonged to that city, not the French capital

explanation.surface: A British government department heading to France's capital spells disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paris' looks like France's capital, but it is the Trojan prince whose city was Troy.
explanation.definitionFit: To ruin something is to wreck or demolish it utterly.

clue.text: Go flat out to produce record sales product

parts.note: REC is an abbreviation for record, as on a recorder button
a line is a type of product a shop stocks and sells

explanation.surface: Rushing at full speed to manufacture a best-selling album.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go flat out' suggests going at top speed, but it means lying flat.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie back horizontally, at rest, is to lean back fully.

clue.text: Area of land fiercely contested by the Crusaders

definitions.meaning: a unit of land measure, 4,840 square yards
the port city in the Holy Land besieged during the Third Crusade

explanation.definitionFit: The unit of land area and the Levantine port city taken by Richard the Lionheart share a spelling.

clue.text: Child recently born to a Spanish princess

parts.note: an infant is a baby or very young child

explanation.surface: A Spanish princess has just given birth.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a birth announcement, but 'Child recently born' is just the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: In Spain and Portugal a daughter of the monarch who is not heir to the throne is so titled.

clue.text: Midas farewell to a retiring employee

definitions.text: Midas farewell to a retiring employee

parts.words: Midas farewell to a retiring employee
parts.note: King Midas turned all he touched to gold, so his parting clasp of the palm would be gilded; the phrase is also a big payoff on leaving a job

explanation.surface: King Midas bids goodbye to a member of staff who is retiring.
explanation.definitionFit: A large lump-sum payment to a departing executive is pictured as a gilded goodbye clasp.

clue.text: They can be climbed by large snakes

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels
adders are venomous snakes

explanation.surface: In the board game, big snakes slither up things meant for climbing.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes the children's board game of snakes and those climbing devices.
explanation.definitionFit: Rungs and rails make a frame people go up step by step.

clue.text: Precise about seeing that the motor has fresh fuel

parts.note: motor is an informal word for a car

indicators.note: fresh suggests the letters of fuel are made new, rearranged

explanation.surface: Being meticulous about checking the vehicle has new petrol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fresh' rearranges FUEL to EFUL, placed after CAR; 'about seeing that the' is link material.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone painstaking and exact in their work takes great pains over details.

clue.text: Cry of pain heard in Oxford University church

parts.note: OU is an abbreviation used for Oxford University

explanation.surface: A scream rings out in an Oxford college chapel.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of sudden hurt, like a yelp when stung.

clue.text: A tiny bit of mottling in the wood

definitions.meaning: a very small particle or trace, as of sand or truth
the pattern of fibres visible on a cut timber surface

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a minute particle and the fibre pattern seen on a plank.

clue.text: Cook needs a slice of the joint

indicators.note: a slice of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A chef requires a cut of the roast meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' suggests a cut of meat for the cook, but it is the leg's hinge.
explanation.definitionFit: The hinge between thigh and shin is a body articulation.

clue.text: Stay on a tender note

parts.note: to tender is to offer, as a bid at auction
E is one of the musical notes

explanation.surface: Remaining on a gentle musical note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tender' looks like 'gentle', but it is an offer, a bid.
explanation.definitionFit: To remain or dwell somewhere is to stay put.

clue.text: Serve up a drink fit for a king

indicators.note: serve up in a down clue asks for the word to be read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: lager is a type of beer

explanation.surface: Pour out a drink worthy of royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Serve up' turns LAGER upward in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal, majestic and splendid enough for a monarch.

clue.text: The chest of long, lanky lad

parts.note: a long, lanky person is tall
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: The torso of a gangly young man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chest' looks like a torso, but it is furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall chest of drawers, often in two stacked sections, is a piece of bedroom furniture.

clue.text: A lotion to relieve conjunctivitis? Bunkum!

definitions.meaning: a soothing liquid for rinsing sore eyes
nonsense, rubbish talk

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an eye-rinsing lotion and nonsense meant to deceive.

clue.text: Leave a lot of players playing

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians
on means in play, as a show that is on

explanation.surface: Departing as a whole crowd of footballers take the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'players' suggests a sports team; here they are musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: To desert or leave behind something for good.

clue.text: Not quite all there? That's rather unfair

definitions.meaning: slightly crazy or eccentric
somewhat unjust or out of order

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase covers both being a little mentally odd and something slightly unacceptable.

clue.text: Unable to compete since the game's been cancelled

definitions.meaning: not equal to a rival, outclassed
literally there is no fixture to be played

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means being outclassed by a rival, and literally that no fixture is happening.

clue.text: Those who are late find only emptied bottles

definitions.meaning: late here means deceased
slang for empty wine or beer bottles after drinking

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both the deceased and empty bottles left after a party.

clue.text: A spider changed this emotion in Robert the Bruce

definitions.text: this emotion in Robert the Bruce

indicators.note: changed tells us to rearrange the letters of the words before it

explanation.surface: Legend says watching a persistent spider transformed the Scottish king's mood.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert the Bruce, Scottish king, hiding in a cave is said to have taken heart from a spider's repeated tries at a web; 'changed' rearranges A SPIDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopelessness is the feeling the legend says the spider lifted from the defeated king.

clue.text: A man of the sea. Right?

definitions.text: A man of the sea. Right?

parts.note: a marine is a soldier serving at sea

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone is truly a seafarer.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines a sailor while also giving MARINE (a sea soldier) followed by R.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailor is a seafarer who works on ships.

clue.text: Former spouse takes Italian vermouth as the way out

parts.note: ex is a former husband or wife
It is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and It

explanation.surface: A divorced partner drinks vermouth as a means of escape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gin and It' is an old British cocktail, gin with Italian vermouth.
explanation.definitionFit: A door marked for leaving a building is the means of departure.

clue.text: Inappropriately made for a single woman

parts.note: Miss is the title of an unmarried woman

explanation.surface: Something unsuitably tailored for an unmarried lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Done wrongly or out of place, as when something goes awry.

clue.text: The arguments in favour of salaried sportsmen

definitions.meaning: the points for
professionals, paid athletes

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both points in favour and paid professionals.

clue.text: Do the French give unemployment benefit?

parts.note: le is the French masculine word for the

explanation.surface: Asking whether the French pay out to the jobless.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for state payments to those out of work.

clue.text: Laos is partitioned too

indicators.note: partitioned suggests the country is broken up and its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: The Southeast Asian country has also been divided.
explanation.definitionFit: Meaning in addition or as well.

clue.text: Cave is an observation post

definitions.meaning: Latin for beware, old British schoolboy slang for a warning cry
a high place used for keeping watch

explanation.definitionFit: The schoolboy warning and a watchtower both mean keeping watch.

clue.text: Greek female runner suffers a loss in Georgia

indicators.note: suffers a loss says the letter A is lost from the runner's name

parts.note: Atalanta was the swift huntress of Greek myth who raced suitors

explanation.surface: A Greek athlete loses a race in the Caucasus country of Georgia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Georgia' looks like the country; it is the US state, whose capital is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital city of the US state is a place found there.

clue.text: A pub-crawl of educational value to the mature student?

definitions.text: A pub-crawl of educational value to the mature student?

parts.words: A pub-crawl of educational value to the mature student?
parts.note: a tour of bars offering a succession of revitalising drinks, punning on a training update for adult learners

explanation.surface: A night out drinking presented as useful for older learners.
explanation.definitionFit: A short training update for experienced workers is pictured as a sequence of reviving drinks.
